name: White Sponge Nevus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological diagnosis of White Sponge Nevus

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral, symmetrical, thickened white plaques on oral mucosa, especially buccal mucosa
Histological findings showing epithelial hyperplasia with perinuclear eosinophilic condensation of keratin tonofilaments
Positive autosomal dominant family history of similar mucosal lesions
Identification of pathogenic variants in keratin genes KRT4 or KRT13

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic bilateral white oral mucosal plaques with confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral symmetrical white spongy plaques on buccal mucosa
searchTerms: white spongy patches inside both cheeks

pathognomonic.symptomName: White thickened plaques on labial and ventral tongue mucosa
searchTerms: white thick plaques on tongue edges and underside

common.symptomName: White plaques on soft palate mucosa
searchTerms: white plaques on soft palate inside mouth

common.symptomName: Lesions present since childhood or adolescence

searchTerms: white mucosal plaques that cannot be scraped off

occasional.symptomName: Mild mucosal erythema adjacent to plaques
searchTerms: slight mucosal erythema adjacent to lesions

occasional.symptomName: Lesions on other mucosal sites such as nasal or esophageal mucosa
searchTerms: lesions on nasal or esophageal mucosa
white patches in nose or throat lining

occasional.symptomName: Plaques with a velvety or folded surface texture

rare.symptomName: Extraoral white plaques on genital mucosa
Secondary candidal infection of oral plaques
Mild oral discomfort or burning sensation

laboratory: Histopathology showing epithelial hyperplasia with perinuclear eosinophilic condensation
Negative fungal cultures unless secondary infection present
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Leukoplakia plaques are usually unilateral and may have dysplastic changes
Leukoplakia often occurs in older adults with risk factors like tobacco use
Candidiasis plaques can be scraped off
Presence of fungal elements on microscopy or culture
Lichen planus presents with reticular white lines (Wickham striae)
Often associated with mucosal inflammation and erosions

redFlags: Rapid progression or ulceration of oral plaques
Presence of dysplastic or malignant transformation
Unilateral lesions or lesions with induration
references: Cannon et al., White Sponge Nevus: Clinical and Genetic Features, Journal of Oral Pathology, 2018
Orphanet Report on White Sponge Nevus, Orphanet 2023
